observation: Frozen donor hidden states indexed by exact ngram suffixes provide a real offline pretrained-to-memory bridge. The demonstrated recipients still train on50B or100B tokens, so cheap adapter-only conversion is unproven.
Engram separates deterministic ngram lookup capacity from contextual computation. Lookup scalability does not establish post-training conversion of an arbitrary pretrained backbone.

STAPLE adds token-indexed residual memory while retaining dense up-projections. Its1B study uses100B warmup plus100B mid-training tokens;7B uses30B plus70B. It preserves rather than removes dense core computation.

MoLE experts consume embedding-layer outputs and can be tabulated by input ID. Released160M/410M-active examples were trained on100B tokens; this is not an exact transformation of context-dependent source experts.
A public68.5B checkpoint assigns over30B parameters to ngram embedding capacity, with approximately3B active parameters. Its remaining decoder core still needs a complete cost screen.
The69B sparse successor selects attention history tokens via indexing; it does not claim that query/output projections are sparse source-head banks.
A real1.6T Switch checkpoint exists, with masked-language-model training and downstream adaptation required. Base checkpoints up to256 experts do not establish fixed-core scaling to C2048.
STEM replaces the FFN up-projection with token-indexed lookup while gate and down remain dense; published350M/1B-scale training is not a pretrained-large-model conversion proof.
